title: AutoRAS: Learning Robust Agentic Systems with Primitive Representations
one_liner: Search over short symbolic building blocks for multi-agent system design, and score those designs using both task success and attack resistance so the final workflow keeps working when parts fail or inputs are adversarial.
lead: Multi-agent systems are usually assembled by hand: choose a set of roles, connect them in some order, and hope the workflow still works when one agent is wrong or when an attacker perturbs the input. This paper automates that design process by representing the whole system as a sequence of symbolic primitives, then learning which primitive sequences produce strong task results and small performance drop under stress.

problem.h2: Why hand-built agent workflows break under stress
paras: A multi-agent system has many design choices: how many agents to use, which role each agent plays, who sends information to whom, and what each step does. People usually choose these pieces manually. That often gives a workflow that looks good on the benchmark it was tuned for, but small disruptions can break it because the design never learned to cope with internal errors or hostile inputs.

The difficult part is that task quality and attack resistance interact. Adding more discussion can help one task because extra review can catch local mistakes, but it can also spread a wrong intermediate result more widely. Adding a checker can catch one failure but slow everything down. The paper reframes the problem as search over a compact design language, because then the system can evaluate many candidate workflows and prefer the ones whose performance degrades less when the environment turns hostile.

callout.html: Represent the agent system as a sequence of symbolic primitives and learn which sequences give high task quality while keeping performance drop small under attacks and internal failures.

steps.text: The system starts from a library of small structural and behavioral actions such as adding a reviewer, routing output, or revising a draft.

steps.b: Encode a workflow as a primitive sequence.
steps.text: Each candidate agent system is written as an ordered list from that library, so the search space becomes explicit and finite.

steps.b: Run the workflow on tasks and stressed variants.
steps.text: Candidates are executed on ordinary tasks and on perturbed settings that contain adversarial inputs or internal failure cases.
The objective rewards high clean-setting task quality and small degradation under stress, because a design is only useful if it keeps working when conditions worsen.
The learner shifts toward primitive sequences that repeatedly earn higher scores across task families because those sequences preserve more task quality under both clean and stressed settings.

paras: The paper changes the unit of design. Instead of choosing a workflow by ad hoc prompting, it builds workflows from explicit primitives that describe both structure and behavior. Once the system design is expressed in that language, the learner can search, compare, and improve full workflows directly because each candidate is written in the same comparable form.
object.object: The system design language: explicit primitive sequences

hidden.h2: The hidden quantity: degradation under stress
hidden.name: Performance degradation under stress
paras: The central hidden quantity is not raw task score by itself. It is how much score is lost when the same workflow faces adversarial inputs or internal faults. Two designs can tie on clean tasks, yet one can collapse under small perturbations while the other loses only a little. That difference is what matters for deployment.

AutoRAS makes this quantity part of the learning signal. The learner observes both clean-setting results and stressed-setting results, then prefers designs whose gap is small. That encourages recovery structure, redundancy, and checking behavior only when those additions actually preserve performance under pressure.

heat.caption: The highlighted cells show where the objective pays most attention: how much quality survives under stress.

reads.html: The hidden quantity is how much performance the workflow loses when the world stops being clean and easy.
The learner optimizes primitive sequences using execution-derived safety signals so that designs with smaller clean-to-stressed performance gaps are favored.

paras: The method works because it gives the search process a compositional language and a stress-aware score. The primitive language makes workflows comparable: one design may differ from another by only one added review step or one changed routing edge, which lets the learner discover which structural choices actually matter. The stress-aware score then keeps the search honest, because a workflow is rewarded only when it performs well and keeps that performance under attack.

This matters more than optimizing clean accuracy alone. If the score ignored stressed settings, the learner would often select brittle workflows that exploit quirks of the benchmark. By including degradation directly in the objective, the search pushes toward designs that contain repair, checking, or diversification only when those components demonstrably preserve output quality.

stages.s: Sample a workflow as a primitive sequence
Run it on clean and stressed settings
Shift search toward sequences with smaller drop

math.words: Score a workflow by its clean-setting result minus a weighted penalty for how much it degrades under stress.
math.equation: objective(workflow) = clean_score(workflow) - lambda * max(0, clean_score(workflow) - stressed_score(workflow))
symbols: task quality on the ordinary benchmark setting
task quality on attacked or failure-prone settings
how strongly the learner penalizes performance drop
counts only positive degradation, not accidental improvement

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Workflow A gets 90 on the clean setting and 50 under attack.
Workflow B gets 86 on the clean setting and 74 under attack.
The learner prefers Workflow B because it keeps more of its quality when conditions worsen.

math.note: The point of the penalty is to reward designs whose quality survives, not designs that look strong only in the easiest setting.

items.html: If the primitive set cannot express useful repair or checking behavior, the search will never discover a strong workflow because the right building blocks do not exist.
If the attacked settings do not resemble real failure modes, the learner may optimize for synthetic tricks instead of genuine system reliability.
If the degradation penalty is too small, brittle high-score designs dominate. If it is too large, the learner can prefer overcautious designs that protect themselves by doing too little useful work.

Use a primitive library that can express real repair behavior, evaluate on realistic stress cases, and tune the degradation penalty so that the search values survivable quality rather than empty caution.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a small agent workflow benchmark with tasks such as answer synthesis or tool-using question resolution. Give the search system a primitive library with roles such as propose, critique, verify, revise, and stop. Compare a hand-built baseline against searched workflows on both ordinary tasks and adversarial variants where one agent receives misleading context or a corrupted intermediate result.
demo.metric_eq: retained_quality = stressed_score / clean_score; improvement = objective_autoRAS - objective_baseline
demo.closing: The demo should show that searched workflows lose less quality under stress because the learning objective rewards designs whose checking and repair structure actually limits degradation.
